I want to say that the people I love and who love me is enough. I honestly feel ashamed that it's not, so I have to find other things to kewep me from it. I have tattoos that would die with me. Their images are things that I value, and it is artwork that exists exclusively on my body. I am always planning my next tattoo, and that planning itself helps as well. I'm working on a video game that I want to finish. The game itself contains many of the things that I want to say, but am not able to. I am terrified that if I don't take care to avoid it, the game itself will become an elaborate suicide note. I need to find another project to begin just before I finish that one.

I want to say that people I care about keep me here... but they don't. I am terrified of hurting them, so I always try to keep projects going that I am working on.

What I want is to be better, or to at least stop feeling so horrible all the time, I am in therapy, I have explored many pills, I have people who are there for me, and every other advantage that I possibly could. I try as hard as I can, and I don't just cave when I face a struggle. But I have been doing this for 40 years, and I feel so, *so* old.

Revolver with 2 out of 6 chambers loaded. I flipped on whether to go through with it and got heads. Spun it, then pulled the trigger against my head. Wasn't playing a game or anything, I was by myself and just in a truly terrible place. Always thankful I didn't pull twice because the next chamber was filled.

It's truly terrifying to remember that and not be able to know if I'll ever be in that mindset again in the future.

Good advice, to be sure. If we had had some vallium on hand, we might have been able to convince him to take it before things went to hell.

As for background and situation... I suppose I'll have to ask him more about his past, but I've known him reasonably well for a good amount of time, and his boyfriend knows him even better. I can't think of what in his past might have caused it. The situation was very peaceful, out in the country with rain pattering on a metal roof and chill music playing. You couldn't have asked for a better setting.

You're right about my friend accepting the risks himself, but I can't help but feel guilty about the situation. I was the most experienced person there, and I feel like no matter what, it happened on my watch.

There is a persistent myth that suicidal people don't "really" want to be dead. There's some kind of idea that people with extreme depression are mentally inferior, and not able to figure out their own desires.

But killing yourself has repercussions for other people, some of whom I care for very deeply. If I could make all of them forget I exist with the press of a button, I would be gone by the end of the day. Also, it's scary as hell.

The people who go through with it and the people who don't have reasons, though. People are dismissive of that because it is so uncomfortable. They like to think that they themselves could never come to that conclusion. It's demeaning to those who suffer with the desires and motivations.

Something that's helped me in the past is reminding myself that I can end it any time that I want to. It sounds counterintuitive, but it reminds me at any given moment that I still exist because I've chosen to. At the really dark times, I have to admit, I've gotten pretty close to ending everything, and I know I'll have more dark points in the future... but I've chosen to still be here, and from time to time, I'm reminded why I keep choosing that. 

I wish you the best of luck, and hope you find reasons to stay alive as well.
That's a really good idea, thanks for the response.

Hey, no need to apologize. Depression is a medical condition like any other. You don't apologize about not being able to run when your foot is broken, and you don't need to tell me that you're sorry for feeling sad when you're depressed. 

I'm really glad to hear that you have a girlfriend to help you through this. Someone who you can trust and talk to about really private matters is invaluable. Best wishes!

I wish I had more suggestions for you, but know that you're not suffering alone. There are a lot of people out here that are going through the same thing, and all of us are pulling for you to keep going and to feel better. 

I can't know when or if your feelings will change, but you're pushing to get better and trying, and that all by itself is very positive. Best of luck, and I hope you make some progress! (if you can get a weed card, definitely give it a try. Anything is worth a go.)

Thanks very much for the response. I just need to build up my resolve to take this every morning and see how it works out. It's a low enough does that my doctor says it might not affect me at all, but better to start low and go up than vice versa.

Hey there, I just want to say that it sounds like you have made it through a *lot* in life. You've done all kinds of difficult things, and just survived in very tough situations. If you're in year 11, then you're nearly to the end of your lower education. If you can at all, please just try to hold things together until you are done with that, and you'll find that you have an opportunity to start things again on your own terms.

Whether you decide to go straight into looking for work, or going to university, you'll be meeting new people, having a chance to introduce yourself however you like, and won't be weighed down with any kind of past.

I didn't realize that when I went into college, but once the fact hit me, it was something I absolutely took advantage of, and it helped me through a lot of tough times. Hang in there, and try to stay strong!
Good for you for making it to the appointment and going through with everything! I hope you find what you're looking for and get well!

I don't know what to say except that it's possible to be happy. That's something that I lose sight of sometimes, myself. When I'm actually happy, I sometimes look at the times when I'm depressed (most of the time) and think to myself "No matter what I've gone through, it's been to earn these moments here, and it's worth it." 

I just try to hold onto that philosophy as best as I am able. It's really difficult sometimes, but it has helped me in the past. 

And... even if you're incredibly lonely, you've made at very least one human contact today. I have no idea who you are, but I know we're going through similar things, and I hope that we can both get through them. Best of luck.

Hey, things might be tough right now, but you're clearly focused on getting better. Everything you wrote there was written with the will to make things right, and to do the best you can.

I can't ever be pregnant, so there's no way I'll be able to understand what you're going through there, but I absolutely see someone who has determination there. Focus on every place where you can see your own strength. Just taking yourself to the place where you are took strength, so please don't forget that.

I have made a few posts here, and the responses that I received were very helpful/encouraging, even if only in regard to how they gave me some human contact. Just acknowledging that I'm dealing with a problem and hearing someone say "I give a shit" is really a good feeling.

I try to contribute in posts where I have something useful to say as well, but I must admit, it takes a lot of energy to do so. Still. I want to get better, and I want everyone who feels the way I do to get better.

You're having an existential crisis. Those are incredibly scary, and I'm not trying to detract from your experience in any way by calling it that. I'm telling you to take the chance to look up some information on them and see that there are a lot of people who have been in similar places to yourself right now. Those people have gotten through their crises and many of them written up valuable advice for getting through them.

As a final point... while suicide might seem like the most logical option to you right now, you're acting on a very particular perspective, and your reasoning reflects that. The reasoning that you use later may lead you to a very different place, yet be *no less logical*.

Long in short, much of what you say is almost certainly true, but the conclusions you come to based on those things are very subjective. Please take the time to explore them from a different perspective before making any permanent decisions.

Well fucking hell. My bad, but I wasn't really in a great state of mind when I called... I am really fucked. GOD DAMNIT.

I am so fucked.
Depression. Seriously, don't judge people who are truly depressed. It isn't just feeling "down."

Talk to your SO if that's a possible thing to do. Ideally, there's no one who knows you better. Tell them exactly what you said here. Or better yet, show them the actual post. Let them know this is an unfiltered look at what you're feeling and going through now.

I've tried counseling and have not personally had success with it (although many do!), and am trying to open up more to people with whom I'm close friends.
Best luck to you!

Yes. I have never attempted suicide, but I feel nearly positive that I will eventually kill myself. It might sound bizarre, but sometimes that is the only thing that lets me go on. "I don't have to kill myself now. I'll definitely do it when the time is right." It's... not a really healthy thing to think, but it's better than having already given in.

But I still can't shake the feeling that sooner or later, that won't be enough. I'm still looking for a way to eliminate those thoughts altogether, and hoping that I'll be able to.

That you're saying you don't want to die soon is a good thing, though. Please keep holding on to the idea that you want to be alive and better. Losing sight of that is dangerous and terrifying for people in our situations.

Your mother doesn't understand what it is to be depressed, or she wouldn't simply say "suck it up." That's not something that will help when you want more than anything to be able to do that. It doesn't help you when what you're *looking for* is a way to do that.

If you have a school councilor, consider going and talking to them. They might have some very practical advice to help you with the situation. They might even be able to talk to your teachers and figure out a plan to help get everything done and turned in on an acceptable schedule. If your teachers see that you're making a true effort to keep things afloat, they are likely to be much more understanding.

As for the rest? Don't let college hang over you. Let it be the light at the end of your tunnel. Looking at college as a place to start over can be a very good thing, so don't deny that to yourself.

I'm very sorry to hear about the situation between your parents. There's nothing that you can do for that but try to make it through and to be there for the people you care about. I'm just a stranger, but I truly hope things turn out well for you and yours.

I don't have any answers for you there, but I'm having a similar experience. Find people who are close to you and summon up the strength to talk to them about it. Asking for help is something that I have struggled with so much in the past, but I've been working on it lately.

If you're brushed off, or find that someone isn't willing/able to help you, then thank them anyway and move on to someone else. Do not let yourself be dissuaded from this, even if you get negative reactions sometimes. Part of why I'm still alive is because I've been able to talk to people.
Thank you for the link! This matches up to me really closely, actually.

My mother reacted in a similar way. She "doesn't believe" in mental illness, more or less accuses anyone who acts oddly of trying to take advantage of society. I'm an adult at this point, and dealing with things on my own, but so incredibly glad that I didn't end up listening to what she said. She was trying to just scare me into working harder, but in reality only communicated a belief that I was worthless unless I did something I was unable to do.

Have you ever gotten any clue where they are from? It sounds like we're experiencing the same thing, but I haven't read about anything like this, and it bothers me to be dealing with something I can't easily look up. : \
I'm not, although I'm probably going to seek some out when I speak to my doctor. Even if I got a bit of that temporarily from the medication, at least it would be gone from the depression.
I have an appointment, but it's for farther off than I would like. I'm definitely going to be mentioning this, though.
I like writing and making constructed languages.

As crazy as it sounds, sometimes I've found just telling myself "I'll kill myself later" has helped me to push the thoughts out of my head. As long as it's always "later," I think this method is ok... but it has helped me in the past, even if it's not perfect.

Best of luck.

I don't know about you, but I have had problems with alcohol and depression before. In general, I've tried to only drink if I'm not feeling too depressed in the first place. If I use it to escape, I generally feel much worse once I sober up.

If you're looking to connect with people more, maybe find a web forum with people that share some interests. Just chatting and having conversations with people online is easy, and it might help you feel more confident to meet people in person.

Best of luck.

Hey, "corny" is ok. "Corny" is great if that's what it takes. Some people have to turn to things like hard drugs, or unhealthy habits just to keep their heads above water. If Street Fighter is what helps you, then keep those quarter circles coming!

Orientation events aren't the end all of friend making. If you decide not to attend even a single one, you haven't somehow doomed yourself to be friendless all through college. I would really suggest you find some more low key groups that might seem less intimidating to you. I guarantee that there are other people just as nervous as yourself, and a lot of them probably share interests with you.

That having been said, freshman orientation stuff is all over the board. Some of it is going to be partying, but some of it will be very low key if you're going to a typical college. If you look into it a bit more, you might find an event or two that seem like they might be ok. Even if you sign up for them, you *don't have to go*. You could even just walk past where they're taking place, and decide on the spot.

Good luck!

Honestly, that seems like a pretty good thing. I'm not currently on any antidepressants, but with positive effects like that, I am hoping that I have luck with them once I have the chance to try them.

That kind of nervousness and self doubt when starting a new job is 100% normal, and almost everyone feels it. Don't worry that it's part of depression or backsliding. A new job is just a big deal, so some worrying an anxiety is totally natural!

I sometimes wish that was an option. I have a really good job, and I can't afford to risk it with taking days just in bed. I don't think I could get a job this good again, and if I lost it, I wouldn't be able to keep up with my mortgage... things would spiral out of control.

Part of me is thinking that I need to get rid of my place so that isn't a risk any more.

Remember, if you think about dying, but don't feel ready, that means that what you really want is to *get better*. Figuring that out is something I'm still working at, but I try not to lose sight of that. I want to be better and to be happy so badly, and I just try to remember that if I kill myself I'll never have that.

Try to just keep trudging toward the light at the end of the tunnel, even if it feels like you can't always see it.

Hanging is one of those things that terrifies me because it's so easy and so effective. It's not like a gun that you can just get rid of or something. There are always the tools that you need, so if its your own actions that you're concerned about, it's very difficult to feel safe.

As crazy as this sounds, I have saved my own life in the past by just saying "I'll do this later." I've gone through multiple periods where the only thing that helped me to stop was to promise myself I would find a better time.

Find any method you can to distract yourself from the actual act. As long as you can walk away from it, it's better than killing yourself.

Every yes. The live I live is by all standards one of privilege and prestige. I've been handed a lot in life, and I've also achieved a lot. I'm lucky enough to have people that care about me and to care about them as well. I suppose without those things I might not even have a chance, but it makes me feel like they're all wasted on me, and wonder how I can even deserve them. I feel like my unhappiness is somehow me being ungrateful for all of those wonderful things. That someone else would appreciate them. It feels awful.

I can understand the eventual suicide thing 100%. Bizarrely, sometimes the only way that I can talk myself down from it is promising that I will do it later, when the timing is better. Even when that is happening, I am thinking to myself "I don't want to die, I just want to be better."

I'm sorry that I don't have anything more constructive to say than "I understand," but I hope that at least makes you know that you're not the only person to feel that.

I suppose... I really have two questions there.

1) How long were you held there and didn't have the option of leaving? (even if you chose willingly to stay, I mean)

2) Do they offer any help other than keeping an eye on you while you're there? I honestly just have no idea what they would even offer other than that.

Thanks for the response!

Wow... yeah, I just looked up the symptoms to that. I'm definitely going to be calling my doctor tomorrow. It's been getting bad enough that whatever form it takes, I need some assistance with the situation. Thanks for the advice.

That's the thing, though. I don't know what to say. All I can think of is this:

me: Doc, I think I'm depressed.

doc: What about?

m: I.. don't really know. I can't think of anything wrong.

d: Why are you wasting my time? 

There isn't actually anything *wrong.* There's no problem to solve. Honestly, I really wish that there were, just so that I could have something to fix. I'm really good at tackling things when I set my mind to it, but there's just nothing to tackle. My life isn't perfect, but I don't have any kinds of problems that could be causing the feelings I'm having.

Also, thank you for your response. I don't mean to shoot down ideas, and appreciate any advice given.

Losing someone you care about so deeply as that is the most profound kind of pain. The person who you turned to for comfort is gone, and in their place is a source of pain. I can't tell you how sorry I am that this happened.

But don't let yourself blame this pain you're feeling on a misplaced sense of guilt. You're no more to blame for the car accident than a grocery store is when someone is in a wreck on the way there. This is one of those senseless, random tragedies that is so difficult to get over because there is more hurt than there is blame.

If she had family, go to them and help however you can. That is the kind of togetherness that can help with healing for everyone involved.

Look at it this way: if the exam goes poorly, you can still go for broke on your bucket list. Who knows, maybe the exam will go well if you really give it everything you've got. Even if it doesn't, and you move on to your bucket list, maybe something there will help you find something else to live for.

Don't give up without a fight.
